case_title: Harjinder Singh v. State of Punjab
statutory_provisions: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to 10 years RI and a fine of Rs. 1 lakh
high_court_outcome: Affirmed the conviction and sentence, but the appeal was set aside and remitted for re-examination
neutral_facts: The accused was convicted under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act for an offence related to narcotics. The trial court sentenced him to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 1 lakh. The accused appealed the conviction and sentence, but during the High Court proceedings, his counsel was absent, and no one appeared on his behalf. The High Court affirmed the conviction and sentence, but the Supreme Court set aside the impugned judgment and remitted the matter back to the High Court for re-examination, giving the accused an opportunity to present his case through a lawyer.
